issue946.title: 8x8 listener inputs 1 to 7 drop every PDU as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT: the monitor context's format is never written for streams above 0
issue946.body:
Found by the flip's gating bench run (#665) on the flip train's final split image (PR #945, `b1f1161b`) at 8x8/1if.

**Defect.** STREAM_INPUTs 1 to 7 bind with SUCCESS and report CONNECTED with the expected current format (`0205022002006000`), but they discard every PDU as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT: FRAMES_RX stays at 0 and MEDIA_LOCKED at 0. The same stream bound to input 0 is received. The CRF input works.

**Cause, by reading the RTL** (not yet measured):
- `KL_avtp_rx_monitor_ctx` checks each PDU against the context's format (`fmt_ok_w`). A mismatch is counted UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT and the PDU is dropped.
- For stream 0 the format is a wired alias of the controller-set format.
- For streams above 0 the format is read from the context RAM's FMT words. The engine writes only stream 0's words. The only other writer is the CSR LCTX window, and no firmware writes it, neither the split's nor the release's.
- The split already publishes each sink's format into the datapath (GET_STREAM_INFO and the audio map use it), but not into the monitor context for streams above 0. So inputs 1 to 7 are compared against a zero format.
- By reading, the all-fabric release behaves the same. The 8x8 config marks streams 2..8 as "planned", but the AEM advertises 8 AAF inputs and ACMP connects them.

**Clauses.** Milan v1.2 Table 5.6 and 4.4.2.2: only a PDU that does not match the current format is UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT. IEEE 1722.1-2021 8.2.

**Related, same area:**
- With two inputs bound to the same talker stream, input 0 stops receiving. This cannot be separated from the above until it is fixed.
- (minor, split) A running output's GET_STREAM_INFO reports `stream_dest_mac` 0 with STREAM_DEST_MAC_VALID set.

**Acceptance.**
- Each of inputs 1 to 7, bound alone, receives: FRAMES_RX rises and UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT stays at 0. All eight inputs bound at once each receive.
- A monitor-context test binds streams above 0 and fails on the current code.
- The bench's stream, power-cycle and soak items pass at 8x8/1if.

Relates to #665
issue946.display_title: 8x8 listener inputs 1 to 7 drop every PDU as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT: the monitor context's format is never written for streams above 0

issue665.title: Mark II split: bare-metal control plane firmware (ADP/ACMP/MAAP/SRP/AECP + saved-state handling) behind the mailbox contract
issue665.body:
## Updated 2026-10-31: owner decisions

- **The protocol processor is removed** (16:33). This firmware becomes the only implementation of ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP, AECP and saved-state handling. No retained-fabric option stays in the end state. The all-fabric default stays only until this firmware passes the bench qualification; at the switch-over `KL_pp_shadow` is deleted.
- **gPTP moves to firmware** (16:51, 17:04), using `flexptpd`, the implementation the test machine runs. Its source and licence get confirmed before adoption: it is not in the public tsn-c-stack repository. The fabric keeps hardware timestamping on both ports. New lane **F6, gPTP**, below.
- **The fabric keeps:** framing and timestamps on both ports, the time-multiplexed stream engines (crossbar, AVTP/AAF endpoints), the media clock, the frame filtering (TCAM and the mailbox ingress filter), the hard-deadline timers, and `milan_csr` for information and diagnostics.
- **Shape: 32x32 streams** (16x16 logical, each redundant on both networks). Every protocol's service-latency bound is stated and tested at this load: four times the 8x8 load, with 64 streams.
- **Area target:** below 20,000 LUTs for the whole image, recorded on #640.
- **Start:** right after the current release tasks (the merge train and the qualification pre-run).

### Lane added

- **F6, gPTP** (IEEE 802.1AS-2011 with Cor1 and Cor2, as profiled by Milan v1.2):
  - `flexptpd` ported to the core behind the HAL, on the fabric's hardware timestamps for both ports;
  - the gPTP qualification and the #117 bench boxes re-run on it;
  - the fast-reaction and GM-recovery directives apply.

### Superseded below

- "The fabric keeps the gPTP plane": the timestamps stay, the protocol moves (F6).
- "Everything lands behind a build switch whose default is the current all-fabric placement": that holds only until the bench qualification of the firmware.

---

## Original text (2026-10-05)

**Owner direction, 2026-10-05:** write the software side of the Mark II split now, in parallel with the protocol-processor program. The requirement change (#664) still waits for the PP program to finish.

## Scope

Bare-metal firmware on the on-chip RISC-V for:
- **ADP**;
- **ACMP** (decided earlier the same day);
- **MAAP**;
- **SRP** (MRP, with MSRP and MVRP);
- **AECP**: descriptor serving, commands, and the unsolicited notifications. The owner added AECP the same day;
- **the NV memory handling**: read the saved entity state from the flash at boot, apply it, and write it back on change (the #70 saved-state design).

It sits behind the packet-mailbox and ingress-filter contract recorded on #640: block RAM rings, doorbell and interrupt, 32-bit accesses, no DMA, a bus adapter per host, portable C behind a small HAL, one YAML contract. It must port to a hard core.

The fabric keeps:
- framing and timestamps;
- the gPTP plane;
- the timers that carry hard deadlines, posted to the core as events;
- the ingress filter.

## Rules while #664 is open

- Everything lands behind a build switch whose default is the current all-fabric placement. No shipping-image change.
- The firmware builds and is tested on the host against a mailbox model. The existing processor suites' stimulus is reused through that model wherever possible, so each protocol's checks carry over.
- Each protocol states its firmware service-latency bound per response path and tests it, as NFR-SCOUT-03 will require after #664.
- Portable C (C11), no compiler intrinsics in protocol code, and a fixed-width, byte-order-explicit wire layer.

## Lanes (in order)

- **F0, the contract and harness (first).** The mailbox and ingress-filter YAML contract and its generator (fabric module skeleton, C header, docs), the HAL, the host mailbox model and test harness. The ADP firmware is the first vertical slice through it.
- **F1, NV memory handling.** Flash read at boot, validation per the #70 saved-state format (KLJ2), apply, and the write and commit path, ported from `sw/firmware/milan_baremetal` and the processor writer's rules. It can start alongside F0 against the HAL draft.
- **F2, MAAP.**
- **F3, ACMP.**
- **F4, SRP (MRP, MSRP, MVRP).**
- **F5, AECP** (descriptor serving, commands, notifications).

F2 to F5 start once F0's contract merges, so the protocols share one interface.

Relates to #640, #664, #70, and milestone 13.

Executor: [A797]. Reviewer: an independent review session, as the maintainer assigns it.
Authoritative references: Milan v1.2 Table 5.6 and 4.4.2.2; IEEE 1722.1-2021 8.2 and 7.4.16; `docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md`, 0x800 window (LCTX words 2/3); the LCTX contract of `KL_avtp_rx_monitor_ctx` (streams above 0 read their format from LCTX w2/w3, which only the window writes).

Stream 0, the mailbox contract, the RTL and the all-fabric image are unchanged. pr.body:
[A797]

## Contents

- **[Status](#status)** — Green/WIP/blocked, test tally, and `branch` -> `dev-soft-core`.
- **[Linked Issue / roles](#linked-issue--roles)** — Public task, executor, and independent reviewers.
- **[Description](#description)** — What changed and why.
- **[Authoritative references](#authoritative-references)** — Requirements/specification clauses and docs.
- **[How to get into the same state](#how-to-get-into-the-same-state)** — Copy-pasteable checkout/dependency/environment commands.
- **[How to validate](#how-to-validate)** — Exact reviewer commands and expected result.
- **[Known limitations / out of scope](#known-limitations--out-of-scope)** — What this deliberately does not do, and why.
- **[Definition of Done](#definition-of-done)** — The merge bar from [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Status

GREEN at `9f4f3de0` (round 2) — `946-ctx-fmt` -> `dev-soft-core`:
- on the branch: the firmware gate (units and every planted-defect campaign), fw_coverage, the platform image's ROM
  ledger with its controls, the memory test, the receive stack's suite, the docs workflow steps that apply to
  dev-soft-core, and the 8x8 split boot simulation; the two-placement simulation reports dev-soft-core's own result;
- on the composition: the same, every docs workflow step, the full sweep (65 of 65 suites), the twin with its plants,
  and the split boot simulation at 8x8 and 1x1.

It composes onto the flip train (PR #945, `b1f1161b`) as step 12 with one composition step. The ROM ledger's files
take the train's side, and the train's `platform-8x8-two-interfaces` entry is raised from 62.5 to 63.0 (below).

Author packets: [`review-evidence/946-r1/author-r1` and `author-r2`](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/946-review-evidence/review-evidence/946-r1) on branch `946-review-evidence` (archive `c6fc4753`).

## Linked Issue / roles

Closes #946
Relates to #665

Executor: `[A797]`
Internal cleared-context reviewer: `[R867]`
External reviewer: `[R868]`

## Description

**The defect (#946, F-G1).** At 8x8/1if, STREAM_INPUTs 1 to 7 bind and report CONNECTED but discard every PDU as
UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT. `KL_avtp_rx_monitor_ctx` judges a PDU of stream 0 against `fmt0_i`, the published format, and a
PDU of any other stream against its LCTX context's FMT_LO/FMT_HI words. The engine writes those words for stream 0
only, and the only other writer is the CSR 0x800 window, which no firmware wrote. So inputs 1 to 7 were compared
against a zero format (Milan v1.2 Table 5.6, 4.4.2.2).

**The fix is firmware-only, in the split platform.** No RTL, no mailbox-contract change, and the AECP face's and the
core's sources are unchanged, so no CPU-budget image moves.

| Piece | Change |
|---|---|
| `plat/ctrl_plat_csr.c`, `.h` | `ctrl_plat_csr_sink_format`: the stream window's listener selection of input n, FMT_LO, FMT_HI, then the selection it held written back. The CSR holds that last write off until the engine took FMT_HI. `ctrl_plat_csr_sink_context`: an AAF STREAM_INPUT above 0 on AVB_INTERFACE 0 in the configuration in force has a context, with its current format. |
| `plat/ctrl_plat.c` | Every AAF input above 0 takes its current format: after `ctrl_app_open_aecp`, every face acknowledged and before ADP starts; then in each change the core keeps, inside the face's change port (wrapped), before the core answers it: a SET_STREAM_FORMAT writes its input's context, a SET_CONFIGURATION every one. The core keeps a change the face applied at once, and one it does again after IN_PROGRESS; the face's applied port, also wrapped, tells the change port which. That applied port answers false for a waiting change that would move the context of an input bound meanwhile, so the core keeps the values in force and answers ENTITY_MISBEHAVING at `AECP_WAIT_MS`, its documented timeout. No poll: no pass with no change writes anything. The state is a file static, so `struct ctrl_plat` and its ledgered size are unchanged. |
| `plat/README.md` | The receive monitor's formats among the ports; the `platsinks` arm among the tests; the 8x8 images' ROM. |
| Tests | `test_plat.cpp` C5 (the window's writes) and C6 (which inputs have a context). `test_plat_sinks.cpp` S1 to S10 at 8x8/1if and 1x1/1if (`plat_arms.arm_platsinks`), every mailbox access watched: whenever an input's binding has a stream published, its context holds the input's current format, from the access that publishes it, and no SET_STREAM_FORMAT's SUCCESS leaves before its context holds it. `sink_mutants.py`: 26 planted defects in the control campaign. |
| RTL contract test | `tb/verilator/avtp_rxmon/sim_ctxfmt.cpp`: the receive stack at the 8x8 shape's eight contexts, [CF1] to [CF5] (96 checks), [CF4] the first PDU after a bind whose format was written the cycle before; `ctxfmt_mutants.py`, 4 planted engine defects; `avtp_rxmon_nx_wrap.sv` sizes its match index by its stream count. |
| ROM ledger | `sw/litex/ctrl_memory.py` LEDGERED: `platform-8x8-two-interfaces` 60.5 -> 61.0, and a new `platform-8x8-one-interface` at 56.5, by the owner's rule of 2026-11-15 (#665); their cases in `ctrl_memory_ledger.py` and `test_ctrl_memory.py`; `plat_ledger.py` links the 8x8/1if point with its entry, with a control for it; `boot_soc.PLATFORM_LEDGERED`; `docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md` sections 3 and 5. |

**Why it is race-free.** A context's format moves only while its input is unbound:

- SET_STREAM_FORMAT and SET_CONFIGURATION refuse a bound input (STREAM_IS_RUNNING).
- A change that waited (IN_PROGRESS) is not applied while an input whose context it moves is bound. A BIND_RX taken during the wait makes that possible. The change stays undone and is answered ENTITY_MISBEHAVING at the wait's bound (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.9; `aecp.h`, `applied`).
- Every change the core keeps writes its contexts in the change port, before the core answers it, with no mailbox access between the change and the write.
- A PDU reaches a context only once its binding's stream_id is published, after the probe's response.

So whenever a stream is published, its context holds the input's current format. An unbind keeps the format: it is
the STREAM_INPUT's, not the binding's. Round 1 said formats move only while unbound; that was false on the deferred
path, where a change waiting for its acknowledgement was done again onto an input bound meanwhile (R868-1-F1). It is
now enforced.

## Authoritative references

- Milan v1.2 Table 5.6 and 4.4.2.2: only a PDU not in the current format is UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT and discarded.
- IEEE 1722.1-2021 8.2 (each sink binds independently), 7.4.9 (SET_STREAM_FORMAT, refused for a bound input) and
  7.4.16 (GET_STREAM_INFO's current format); Table 7-126 (IN_PROGRESS, ENTITY_MISBEHAVING, STREAM_IS_RUNNING).
- IEEE 1722-2016 Table 6 (the AAF subtype).
- `docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md`, the 0x800 stream window (LCTX words 2 and 3).
- `hdl/ieee1722/avtp/KL_avtp_rx_monitor_ctx.sv` (the LCTX record and its window port contract), `aecp/aecp_face.h`
  (`applied`), `aecp/aecp.h` (`AECP_WAITS`, `AECP_WAIT_MS`, a waiting change done again or kept undone).
- The owner's decision of 2026-11-15 on #665 (issuecomment-6892332745): an image past its ROM entry raises it to its
  measured half tile, as named debt owed to S14.

## How to get into the same state

```sh
git fetch origin 946-ctx-fmt dev-soft-core
git checkout 946-ctx-fmt
git submodule update --init gptp-processor protocol-processor third_party/lwSRP third_party/tsn-c-stack third_party/verilog-axis
# the repository's pinned toolchain and RV32 SDK (sw/firmware/gtest/README.md, docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md)
```

## How to validate

```sh
# the firmware: units, every arm, and the planted-defect campaigns (platsinks among them)
python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test
python3 sw/firmware/gtest/fw_coverage.py --check
# the platform image at every ledger point, and the memory test's ledger cases
python3 tb/verilator/ctrl_split_boot/plat_ledger.py --build-dir <dir> --self-test
python3 sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py
# the receive stack's suite, the N=8 format contract and its planted engine defects among it
make -C tb/verilator/avtp_rxmon
# the two-placement simulation and its plants
make -C tb/verilator/milan_dp twin twin-plants
```

Expected result / pass criteria:
- every arm PASS; `Sinks.S1` to `S10` and `Plat.C5`, `C6` pass at both shapes;
- the campaign reports every defect caught, the 25 `sink-*` and `set-format-bound-accepted` among them;
- `plat_ledger: PASS (0 finding(s))` with every control as required, and `test_ctrl_memory: 0 failure(s)`;
- `CTXFMT N=8: 96 checks, 0 failures` and `5 checks: 5 PASS, 0 FAIL`;
- the twin's plants each refused by their words.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- **F-G2 (one stream bound to two inputs) is #948.** The stream parser classifies a PDU to one context, the
  highest matching enabled entry (`avtp_stream_parser.sv:193-196`), so with this fix the higher input receives and
  the lower one still does not. Fan-out needs RTL and a ruling.
- **The release image's F-G1 is #949.** The all-fabric image shares the zero-format defect and is unchanged here: its
  firmware writes none of these words, and its AECP is the fabric's, so a firmware write could not follow
  SET_STREAM_FORMAT; the fix there is RTL. #946's scope is the split image.
- **F-G3 (a running output's `stream_dest_mac` 0) is #943's**, the datapath's GSI face; unchanged here.
- **A change that waited, refused because its input was bound meanwhile, is answered ENTITY_MISBEHAVING** at the
  wait's bound (100 ms after the command), the core's documented answer for a change not applied, not
  STREAM_IS_RUNNING: the core's sources are unchanged.
- **The datapath's copy of the face during that wait.** The face committed the change before the core undid it, and
  the datapath takes that commit when it acknowledges it. So until the face publishes the values in force again, its
  per-input format (`F_FMT_IN`, the map's channel clip for inputs above 0) may hold the refused value. The face's
  existing rollback path ends this, at most the wait's bound.
- **Input 0, the CRF input and STREAM_OUTPUTs have no context here.** For those, the core still does a waiting change
  again without repeating its bound or running check (`aecp.c`, the waiting command); for input 0 the face's own
  commit carries the format to `fmt0_i`. Repeating the check there is the core's own change, which moves every
  CPU-budget image. It is not this issue's receive-context defect; a ticket of its own is proposed.
- **ROM, by the owner's rule of 2026-11-15** (debt owed to S14):
  - On dev-soft-core the platform's 8x8/2if image plans 61.0 RAMB36: 133,224 B of rom, 104 B past the 133,120 B
    that 60.5 holds. Its entry is raised from 60.5 to 61.0.
  - Its 8x8/1if image, a product image, plans 56.5: 131,656 B, 584 B past 56.0. It takes its own entry,
    `platform-8x8-one-interface`, at 56.5.
  - On dev-soft-core the product SoC build names no entry, so an 8x8/1if product build there is still held to 56.
    The flip train plans product images at their own entry (`own_point`).
  - **At composition onto the train**, these ledger files conflict with the train's. They take the train's side,
    where `platform-8x8-one-interface` is already 58.0 and the composed 8x8/1if image fits it at 138,624 B. The
    train's `platform-8x8-two-interfaces` entry is raised from 62.5 to 63.0: the composed image plans 140,200 B of
    rom, 936 B past the 139,264 B that 62.5 holds.
- The platform's new work runs only in the product image, which no CPU-budget row measures; the rows' images are the
  size fixture's and are byte-identical to the train's recorded ones (1x1 `55484254e638ed7f`, 8x8/1if
  `175418f4b5b1a9d4`). In the split boot simulation on the composition at 8x8, the product image writes the seven
  contexts before ready: 28 window writes in 3,022 bus cycles. It reaches ready at 67.328 ms against the train head's
  67.134. At 1x1 it writes nothing and reaches ready at 27.936 ms against 27.981; that run does strictly more work yet
  is sooner, so these figures bound the cost and do not resolve it below a few thousand cycles. Neither is near the
  20,000 ms bound.
- At dev-soft-core alone the two-placement simulation reports the owed row `split-talker-failed`, and its plant
  `srp-plus-k` escapes, exactly as dev-soft-core `cb96336d` does with byte-identical captures. The flip train restates
  that row; on the composition the twin reports 0 findings and refuses every plant.
- The register map's design note for FMT_LO/FMT_HI lives in the train's regenerated reference; who writes these words
  is documented in `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/README.md`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Linked Issue acceptance criteria are satisfied (the bench's stream, power-cycle and soak items at 8x8/1if are
      the gating run's, after this change is composed)
- [x] New or changed behavior has self-checking tests
- [ ] Required local verification bar passes
- [ ] Self-test evidence is posted in a PR comment
- [x] No undocumented requirement or interface change remains
- [ ] Internal cleared-context review is positive
- [ ] External review is positive
- [ ] Blocking and major findings are fixed and re-reviewed
- [ ] No review round remains in flight
- [ ] Candidate merge result is validated per [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Documentation is updated where needed
- [ ] Post-merge containment will be checked before the Issue moves to Done

followups.title: 8x8: two STREAM_INPUTs bound to one talker stream: the parser hands each PDU to one context only, so the first input stops receiving
followups.body:
Found by the flip's gating bench run (#665) at 8x8/1if, next to #946.

**Defect.** When two of the entity's STREAM_INPUTs are bound to the same talker stream (for example input 0 and input 1), input 0 stops receiving. It receives again once the other input is unbound. IEEE 1722.1-2021 ACMP lets each sink bind independently, so one stream_id can be the source of several of an entity's inputs.

**Cause, by reading** (the #946 lane): the AVTP receive parser hands each PDU to one monitor context only, the highest-numbered matching input. A second binding to the same stream therefore takes the PDUs away from the first. Fixing it means a datapath (RTL) change that fans one PDU out to every context bound to that stream_id.

**Open question for the ruling:** whether fan-out of one stream to two inputs of the same entity is required for the Mark II scope, or whether the entity should refuse the second bind (and with which ACMP status).

Relates to #946
Relates to #665

followups.title: Release (all-fabric) image: STREAM_INPUTs above 0 would drop every PDU as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, as #946 found in the split
followups.body:
The all-fabric release image has the same defect #946 fixes in the split image: STREAM_INPUTs above 0 would discard every PDU as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT. Their receive-monitor context format words are never written, because no release firmware writes the CSR LCTX window and the engine writes only stream 0's words.

This is by reading only; no all-fabric 8x8 image has been benched. #946's fix (PR #947) is firmware in the split platform and leaves the release image byte-identical, so the release needs its own fix. Either the release firmware writes the window as the split platform now does, or the engine writes each context's format on the bind edge (RTL).

**Acceptance.** On an all-fabric 8x8 image, each input above 0 bound alone receives (FRAMES_RX rising, UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT 0), with a test that fails on the current code.

Relates to #946
Relates to #665

priorFindings.body:
## Findings

### R868-1-F1 - MAJOR - Conformance, RTL, Robustness, Tests, Docs

**Artifact:** `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/ctrl_plat.c:178` and `:193`; related `sw/firmware/ctrl/aecp/aecp.c:906`, `sw/firmware/ctrl/app/ctrl_app_aecp.c:10`, `third_party/tsn-c-stack/src/acmp.c:883`; missing interleaving in `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_plat_sinks.cpp:443`; incorrect invariant at `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/README.md:86` and `ctrl_plat.c:140`.

**Title:** A bind can settle during IN_PROGRESS, leaving its published stream active while current format and LCTX disagree.

**Authority/evidence:** #946's race-free scope; Milan v1.2 Table 5.6 / 4.4.2.2; the SET/GET_STREAM_FORMAT and binding contracts, IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.9 / 7.4.10 and 8.2; AGENTS.md section 6. The bound-input refusal checks binding at the original dispatch. A deferred command later swaps its saved change back in without repeating that check. ACMP reads the entity lock; a pending format change does not prevent BIND_RX or its probe response. The new writer supplies no serialization with that binding.

The reviewer probe uses unchanged production firmware with one additional host-composition test. It sends SET_STREAM_FORMAT for input 7, holds acknowledgement until IN_PROGRESS, sends BIND_RX, answers the actual emitted PROBE_TX with its sequence number, waits for settlement, then acknowledges the face:

```text
STALE: bound=1 published_sid=5544332211002233 current=0205022000806000 LCTX=0205022002006000
PROBE: input=7 bound=1 settled=1 final_status=0 old=0205022002006000 current=0205022000806000 window=0205022000806000
```

Three mailbox reads observe the new current format while the settled binding remains published and LCTX holds the old format. Eventually LCTX catches up and SET_STREAM_FORMAT returns SUCCESS. The original five tests pass in the same run; the added named coherence assertion fails, exit 1. Receipts: `deferred-bind.log`, `deferred_bind.cpp`, `probe_deferred_bind.py`. The observer only reads state and does not alter firmware behavior.

**Impact:** The documented statement that formats move only while unbound is false. During the observed interval a PDU for the published binding may encounter the previous channel count. The unchanged monitor compares against those words (`KL_avtp_rx_monitor_ctx.sv:1001` / `:1011`); consequently a PDU matching the new current format can be discarded as UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT. That packet consequence follows from the independently exercised RTL comparator. The probe does not claim to have measured the transient on hardware or in combined CPU/datapath simulation. Write arbitration prevents a lost write, but does not provide binding/format atomicity.

**Required outcome:** Serialize pending format transitions with bind/settle publication, or demonstrate another ordering that keeps active binding, current format and monitor context coherent. Preserve bounded responses, timeout rollback and the mailbox contract. Correct the documented race argument. Retaining only the initial bound-input refusal, or moving this finding to another issue, does not resolve it.

**Verification:** Add delayed acknowledgement plus bind plus successful probe, including timeout and rebind variants. Check coherence while a nonzero SID is published and exercise the first matching PDU at that boundary. Existing S2 binds before a later command; S4 has no competing bind and waits 20 extra passes before checking. Neither covers this order. Re-run the firmware and engine plants after the fix.

All five lenses apply: protocol/current-format correctness; firmware/datapath ordering; delayed acknowledgement with concurrent traffic; missing cross-protocol test; and a new false documentation claim. The documentation defect is substantive, not RESIDUE.

### R868-1-R1 - RESIDUE - Docs

**Artifacts:** `tb/verilator/avtp_rxmon/sim_ctxfmt.cpp:5`, `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_plat_sinks.cpp:6`.

**Authority/evidence:** Supplied owner source-comment rule, 2026-10-15: behavior/reason and issue/requirement identifiers, without lane names. New comments say `lane-A stack` and `F1's flash model`.

**Impact:** Wording only; no code, measurement, verdict, clause interpretation or privacy change.

**Exact fix:** Replace `the lane-A stack of avtp_rxmon_nx_wrap` with `the receive stack of avtp_rxmon_nx_wrap`; replace `F1's flash` with `the saved-state flash`. Keep module names and #946/clause references.

**Verification:** Inspect the added lines and confirm a comment-only diff. This residue does not itself leave a lens unclean.

## Findings

### F-1 MINOR — Docs, Tests — `sw/litex/ctrl_memory.py` LEDGERED / `docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md` §5 / `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/README.md:123` — ROM entries not raised as the owner's 2026-11-15 rule requires; the ledger check turns red
- **Authority / evidence:** The owner's decision of 2026-11-15 (#665 `issuecomment-6892332745`): "An image past its entry raises the entry to its measured size, at the next half tile, as named debt owed to S14". `plat_ledger.py` passes at base and fails at head: 8x8-if1 56.5 RAMB36, and `ctrl_plat_image.py` exits 2 "allocation over budget". On the composition it fails at 8x8-if2: 63 past the 62.5 entry, link refused. Receipts: `plat_ledger_{base,head,composition}.log`. The lane deliberately leaves the ledger untouched (PR body, "ROM"). `plat/README.md:123`, in the file this PR edits, still says "Every other point is within 56", which is false at this head.
- **Impact:** On dev-soft-core the 8x8/1if product image, the shape this fix targets, is refused at link. On the train composition the 8x8/2if product image is refused. An existing green check becomes red, and the authoritative memory document and README carry stale figures.
- **Required outcome:** Each image past its entry has the entry raised to its measured half tile as named S14 debt, with the ledger record (`ctrl_memory.LEDGERED`/`ctrl_memory_ledger.py`), SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY §5 rows and README statement current. Two ways satisfy this: on the lane for dev-soft-core's 8x8/1if (56.5), or as a publicly recorded step of the train composition that raises `platform-8x8-two-interfaces` to 63.0, with the lane only ever landing through the train.
- **Verification:** `plat_ledger.py --self-test` PASS on the lane head and on the composition. README/§5 figures match its POINT lines.

### F-2 MINOR — Tests, Robustness — `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/ctrl_plat.c:196-198`, `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_plat_sinks.cpp:480-508` — the poll's owed-flag clearing has no test; a poll that rewrites every context on every pass escapes
- **Authority / evidence:** AGENTS §6 Tests and Robustness (repeated commands and idempotence; each test can fail for the defect it claims to cover). The README's new claim at `README.md:84` reads "The poll's own share is one comparison a pass". Reviewer plant R2 removes `sinks.owed = false;` from `plat_poll`. Every `plat`/`platsinks` check still passes (0 failed): `extra_probes_head.log`. S5 checks only that the words written since `from` hold the format in force, never that the rewrite happens once.
- **Impact:** After the first deferred change (SET_NAME, a lock, IDENTIFY, a STREAM_OUTPUT format), the product loop would rewrite all seven contexts on every pass. That is 35 window accesses plus a descriptor scan per pass, about 0.1 ms at 8x8 by the boot receipt. No CPU-budget row measures the product image (PR body says so), so neither the suites nor the budget harness would see the regression.
- **Required outcome:** A check that a deferred change is written once: for example, after S5's rewrite, further loop passes make no window write. That defect is then added to `sink_mutants.py`.
- **Verification:** The R2 plant (or its equivalent) is caught by its named test on its own words.

### F-3 MINOR — Docs, Conformance — PR #947 body "Known limitations" and issue #946 — follow-up tickets for F-G2 and the release image's F-G1 not filed while the PR says `Closes #946`
- **Authority / evidence:** AGENTS §4: newly discovered work becomes another public Issue. The PR names two items "for its own ticket": F-G2, one stream bound to two inputs, an RTL cause at `avtp_stream_parser.sv:189-199`; and the all-fabric image sharing the Table 5.6 defect, whose fix is RTL. An issue search on 2026-11-18 finds neither. #946 is their only public record. #943 exists for F-G3.
- **Impact:** Closing #946 leaves a known Milan v1.2 Table 5.6 non-conformance in the release image, and the F-G2 fan-out defect, with no open work item.
- **Required outcome:** Both issues are filed and linked from #946/#947, or #946 stays open naming them, before #946 closes.
- **Verification:** Both issue links are present on #946 and #947.

### R-1 RESIDUE — Docs — `tb/verilator/avtp_rxmon/sim_ctxfmt.cpp:5` — a work-lane name in a new source comment
- "the lane-A stack of avtp_rxmon_nx_wrap": "lane A" is a work-lane name (`docs/history/v1/NXN_ARCHITECTURE.md:929`). The owner's comment rule (2026-10-15) applies; the existing instances in the wrapper and `sim_main_nx.cpp` are tracked by #746. Exact fix: "the multi-stream RX stack of avtp_rxmon_nx_wrap".

No other wording defect was found in the delta's source comments: no bench label, reviewer ID, round or comment ID.
